title: M7 states the finite-type geometry of SPEC 2.14 for every board, and its verification for 'every board of rank two to eight'
location: site/src/content/modules/m7-geometry.mdx, route /modules/m7-geometry/: beat 2; beat 6; Seen bullets 1, 2 and 4
claim: M7 drops the finite-type hypothesis that SPEC 2.14 places on its geometry. Beat 2 says 'Free play from the position reaches finitely many positions, its orbit, whose convex hull is a polytope', and Seen 2 says 'The orbit of a position with no negative number is the vertex set of a polytope whose shape depends only on the ringed nodes'. Neither sentence restricts the board, and both are false off the finite types. Beat 6 and Seen 1 and 4 give the verification as 'verified by computation ... every board of rank two to eight'.
expected: SPEC 2.14: 'Euclidean coordinates (finite type)'; the recipe is '[V for every type of rank 2 to 8; oracle function euclidean_basis]'; the Coxeter-plane facts are '[V for every type of rank 2 to 8]'. SPEC 0.3: the range of boards checked is part of the claim. SPEC 2.7: 'Finite type means one of the boards of section 2.8'. Precedents: round 1 P3-RT-09-02 and P3-RT-09-07.
observed: On the triangle A2~ (rank 3, roads both ways, affine by classify), free play from (1,0,0) passes 5000 positions (engine orbit truncated; oracle orbit(..., cap=5000) raises OverflowError). The orbit is infinite, so it is the vertex set of no polytope. On the same board the form is singular ((1,1,1) has form value 0; eigenvalues of D^1/2 C D^-1/2 are 0, 3, 3), there is no Coxeter number and no Coxeter plane, and the engine's euclideanBasis throws NotFiniteType. Nothing in 2.14 was verified there. golden types[T].coxeter_plane covers the 31 finite types of rank 2 to 8 only.
reproduction: From a clean checkout of b9b8504 plus the reproducer: npm ci --prefer-offline; npx vitest run --project site-unit site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-09-p4-m7-finite-type.test.ts. Result: test 1 passes (the five sentences are on the page and beat 2 never says 'finite type'); tests 2 and 3 fail (orbit truncated at 5000 on the triangle; euclideanBasis throws NotFiniteType). Oracle: python3 redteam/RT-09/redteam-RT-09-p4-oracle.py reference (lines M7-b6-triangle, M7-b2-triangle-orbit, INFO M7-triangle). Preview build.
specRef: SPEC 2.14 (Euclidean coordinates '(finite type)'; '[V for every type of rank 2 to 8]'); 2.7 opening; 0.3; lens attacks 1, 25 and 29. Oracle: cartan_class(triangle)='affine'; orbit(triangle, [(1,0,0)], fire, cap=5000) raises OverflowError.
proposedFix: Add 'on a board of finite type' to beat 2 and Seen 2. In beat 6 and Seen 1 and 4, write 'on every board of finite type of rank two to eight'.

title: Attack 16, sibling of P3-RT-08-01: M7 says its geometry facts were 'verified by computation on every board of rank two to eight'; the check covered only the finite types
claim: M7 extends the check of SPEC 2.14 to every board of rank 2 to 8. That includes affine and indefinite boards, where neither statement can hold.
expected: SPEC 0.3 [V]: 'the range of boards checked is stated with the claim or is "every type of rank at most 8"'. SPEC 2.14: '[V for every type of rank 2 to 8; oracle function euclidean_basis]' and, for the Coxeter plane, '[V for every type of rank 2 to 8]'. The site should say 'every board of finite type of rank two to eight'.
observed: Beat 6: 'No root lands on the centre, and the roots lie on circles each holding a multiple of h of them, verified by computation on every board of rank two to eight.' Seen box: 'The coordinates y=Ep with E^TE=B make the form the dot product: verified by computation, every board of rank two to eight.' and '... its circles hold multiples of h roots, none at the centre: verified by computation, every board of rank two to eight.' A counterexample of rank 2: on the board with three roads each way (golden layer_growth_examples), det C = 4 - 9 < 0. So B = DC has a negative eigenvalue, no real E with E^TE = B exists, and there is no Coxeter number.
reproduction: npm ci && npx vitest run site/tests/unit/redteam-RT-08-p4-rank-range.test.ts (fails on the source test, listing lines 114, 156, 159)
specRef: SPEC.md 0.3 [V] row; 2.14 'Euclidean coordinates' and 'The Coxeter plane' [V for every type of rank 2 to 8]; 8.4 'Verified by computation for all boards of rank at most 8' (the range stated); lens attack 16
proposedFix: Write 'verified by computation on every board of finite type of rank two to eight' in the three places.

title: M7's b12 challenge rejects a right answer: the rings (2, 1, 0) on B3 give 24 vertices and 36 edges, but the check accepts only (1, 1, 0)
location: site/src/content/modules/m7-geometry.mdx, Challenge for b12 (route /modules/m7-geometry/); check { kind: 'out', name: 'polytopeName', equals: 'truncated octahedron' }
claim: The goal is 'Find rings on B3, other than those of beat 5, that also give 24 vertices and 36 edges.' The check reads T10's polytopeName. T10 names a polytope only for the exact rings of a golden wythoff record (t10/names.ts POLYTOPE_NAMES, keyed by '<type>:<rings>'), so the check is met by (1, 1, 0) alone (decisions/P4-A6.md: 'the name check is met only by B3 (1, 1, 0)'). Rings such as (2,1,0) or (1,2,0) satisfy the goal as printed, and M7 itself says the shape 'depends only on which nodes are ringed'. The challenge never reports success for them.
expected: SPEC 4.0 Predict and 8.5 (a challenge 'says when its goal is reached'); lens attack 16 ('reach the goal by a legitimate play and by a near miss, and read whether the check reports success'). SPEC 2.14: 'whose combinatorics depend only on which nodes are ringed'. Oracle: wythoff_f_vector(cartan('B',3), [2,1,0]) = [24, 36, 14, 1], the same as for [1,1,0].
observed: On the built page, b12 was played from (0,1,1) to (1,1,1), then (2,1,1) (Ring 1 up), then (2,1,0). It showed vertexCount 24, edgeCount 36, fVector '24, 36, 14' and edgeLengths '4, 16'.
